name: ODDFPRICE
description: ODDFPRICE returns the price per $100 face value of a bond that has an irregular first coupon period.
tldr: Calculates the price of a security with an odd first coupon period.
syntax: (settlement, maturity, issue, first_coupon, rate, yld, redemption, frequency, [basis])

parameters.name: first_coupon
parameters.description: Date of the first coupon payment.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Number of coupon payments per year (1, 2, or 4).

basicExample.description: Price of a bond with an odd first coupon period
basicExample.explanation: Calculates the price of a bond issued January 1, 2024 with a first coupon on July 1, 2024.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/actual basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 1 is common for Treasury bonds.

howItWorks: ODDFPRICE handles bonds where the first coupon period is longer or shorter than a standard coupon period. It adjusts the price to account for the irregular accrual period.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: All dates must be valid Excel dates.
The first coupon date must be after the issue date but before maturity.

commonErrors.fix: Verify the date order and that all inputs are valid.
Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ODDFPRICE works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is an odd first coupon period?
faq.answer: It is a first coupon period that is not a standard length because the bond was issued on an off-cycle date.

faq.question: When is ODDFPRICE used?
faq.answer: It is used for new bond issues that settle between coupon dates.
